mainEntity.name: Why is SSA called the ambiguous case?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the sine function gives the same value for an acute angle and its supplement (sin θ = sin(180° − θ)), the known angle can be met by an acute or an obtuse angle B. When h < a < b both are valid and two different triangles fit the data.

mainEntity.name: What is Heron’s formula and when is it better than ½ × base × height?

acceptedAnswer.text: Heron’s formula gives the area from the three sides alone: K = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], with s the semi-perimeter. It is convenient when you know all three sides but no height or angle.

mainEntity.name: What makes three side lengths a valid triangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: The triangle inequality: each side must be shorter than the sum of the other two. If the longest side equals the sum of the other two the triangle is degenerate (a flat line), and if it is longer no triangle exists.

mainEntity.name: How do I convert between degrees, radians and gradians?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full turn is 360° = 2π radians = 400 gradians. So radians = degrees × π ÷ 180 and gradians = degrees × 10 ÷ 9. The angle-unit switch on this page converts your inputs and results for you.

mainEntity.name: Why can’t three angles alone determine a triangle?

acceptedAnswer.text: Any triangle scaled up or down keeps the same angles, so AAA describes a whole family of similar triangles. You need at least one side to fix the size.
By sides it is equilateral (all equal), isosceles (two equal) or scalene (none equal). By angles it is acute (all below 90°), right (one exactly 90°) or obtuse (one above 90°).
